doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing with Chick Corea at the new Yoshi's
summary: Brown recalls hearing Laws, Chick, Eddie Gomez and Airto open the new Yoshi's in San Francisco. Laws praises the hall.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Just as an aside or a footnote, I saw you come through when Chick came to Yoshi’s, San Francisco – when they first opened up Yoshi’s – as a quartet.
You’re talking about the new one?
Yeah, that was about two or three years ago.
Yeah. It was a quartet: you, Chick, Eddie Gomez, and Airto.
I said, oh, Hubert. Hubert stole the show. Between you and Eddie, you all stole the show.

I know, but we all know Chick’s going to do that, but we didn’t know, in a quartet – we knew Chick was going to show, but you definitely held your own, and Eddie took some solos that were just amazing.
Yeah, Eddie’s just – I told you, his mic was turned way up. I wish I could get them to turn my mic up that strong.

I remember that gig specifically because you were getting slapback, because they hadn’t really tuned the sound system, because it was so new. The hall just opened up. Chick was really trying to get them to get the sound right.
Yeah, that’s a nice hall. I like that. Really well designed.
